## ggplot: Questions {.unnumbered}

Load the ggplot2 library (install it if you have to) and the diamonds data set using data()

```{r, eval=F}
# if needed install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)
data("diamonds")
```

::: panel-tabset
### Question 1

Explore the data set using dim(), str() and help(), which variables are continuous, which variables are discrete? Is this data set ready for plotting with ggplot?
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 2

Use ggplot to make a scatterplot of diamond price versus carat.
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 3

Make all dots darkblue and set the alpha value to 0.1
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 4

Visualize the influence of the color of a diamond on its price by mapping the diamond color to the color aesthetic

### Hint

Question 3 used a single colour for every point. Here a column controls colour, so put the colour mapping inside `aes()`.
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 5

Use a ggplot barplot to visualize diamond clarity depending on color, map diamond color to x and diamond clarity to fill
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 6

Create a boxplot of the carat of a diamond based on its clarity and add whiskers using stat_boxplot

### Hint

Map the grouping variable to `x` and the measurement to `y` in `ggplot()` so both layers inherit them. The boxplot already draws whiskers. Use `stat_boxplot()` with the `errorbar` geometry to add the caps.
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 7

Add a geom_point layer to the previous plot mapping the diamonds price to the color
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 8

Create a histogram of the price of the diamonds and separate the histograms into facets using diamond color, choose a good binwith or number of bins

### Hint

Build one histogram first. Then use `facet_wrap()` to split it by colour and keep the same bin width across panels so the shapes are easier to compare.
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 9

Create a grid of facets of the same histogram by comparing both color and cut

### Hint

Keep the histogram layer from Question 8. In a `facet_grid()` formula, the variable on the left of `~` defines the rows and the variable on the right defines the columns.
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 10

Use `aggregate()` to calculate the mean price for each combination of cut and colour. Create a heatmap of those means with `geom_tile()`.

### Hint

Before plotting, check that your summary has one row per cut and colour combination. In the formula interface to `aggregate()`, put the measurement on the left of `~` and join the grouping columns with `+` on the right. Which column should control each tile's fill?
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 11

Change the title of the heatmap to "Average prices"
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 12

Change the gradient of the fill scale using 'scale_fill_gradient2'. Have it go from darkblue to white to darkred, set the midpoint to 4500

### Hint

Add the scale to the heatmap with `+`. The three colour arguments are `low`, `mid`, and `high`. `midpoint` is a value on the price scale, so the middle colour should correspond to a price of 4500.
:::

::: panel-tabset
### Question 13

Choose and add a theme to the heatmap, or create a theme yourself using the options listed at <http://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/theme.html>
:::
